2608.25976.title: Lost but not erased: Finding traces of a forgotten language in neural speech models
2608.25976.paper_summary: International adoptees retain phonological traces of a birth language they can no longer speak or comprehend, a persistence typically attributed to a biologically-timed critical period. We asked whether it could instead reflect the ordinary dynamics of learning, using automatic speech recognition models that simulate the international adoptee experience without maturational confounds. Models were trained on one language and then abruptly switched to a second. We found that traces of the first language persisted throughout second-language training, but mainly in the lowest, pre-phonemic layers. These traces were functional, as models with early exposure re-learned their lost first language 14% faster than naive models; this advantage held even against models adopted early from a related language and disappeared when the earliest layers were substituted from a non-adopted model. We argue that these critical-period effects reflect entrenchment of foundational representations rather than a maturational loss of plasticity, and that experience plays a central role in critical periods in language acquisition.
2608.25976.paper_summary_zh: 國際收養者保留著他們已經無法說或理解的母語的音韻痕跡，這種持續性通常被歸因於生物學上定時的關鍵期。我們詢問這是否可能反映學習的普通動態，使用自動語音識別模型來模擬國際收養者的經歷，而不受成熟混淆的影響。模型在一種語言上進行訓練，然後突然切換到第二種語言。我們發現第一語言的痕跡在第二語言訓練過程中持續存在，但主要集中在最低的前音位層。這些痕跡是功能性的，因為早期接觸的模型以比天真的模型快14%的速度重新學習了他們失去的第一語言；這一優勢甚至在與早期從相關語言收養的模型相比時也依然存在，並且當最早的層被非收養模型的層替代時消失。我們認為這些關鍵期效應反映了基礎表徵的鞏固，而不是成熟性塑性喪失，並且經驗在語言習得的關鍵期中扮演著核心角色。
